answer:
RECOMMENDATION: two building records, not one, joined by a single 1938 event.

Record the barn described in the 1839 tithe survey and the barn now standing at Combe Farm as two distinct instances of E24 Physical Human-Made Thing, and join them with one 1938 event instantiated both as E81 Transformation and E12 Production. The event P124 transformed the Hollow Farm barn and P123 resulted in / P108 has produced the Combe Farm barn. Strictly, the CRM's answer is neither of the two options the question offers: the Combe Farm barn is a new unit of documentation, but it is not merely 'a new building that reuses material' either, because the physical continuity with the 1839 barn is carried explicitly by the event that links the two records. As the Issue 404 text puts it, 'The physical continuity between the old and the new is expressed by the link to the common Transformation'.

WHY THIS AND NOT ONE CONTINUING BUILDING

1. E81's scope note names this case. It covers events that destroy one instance of E18 Physical Thing and create another that preserves recognisable substance and structure but has fundamentally different nature or identity, and it states that 'Characteristic cases are reconstructions and repurposing of historical buildings or ruins' (that sentence is the Issue 404 text, verified in t1396; it stands in the current E81 scope note).

2. E24's scope note supplies the test, and it is a closed decision (Issue 386, closed June 2020). Where a thing is made by modifying pre-existing material and preserving much of the original matter and structure, the interventions must be obvious and sufficient for the product to count as having a new, distinct identity and intended function; and it directs that substantial continuity of the previous matter and structure be documented by describing the production also as an E81 Transformation. Total dismantling, a new brick plinth, a new roof covering, one bay renewed outright, and re-erection on a different site four miles away clears that bar comfortably.

3. E6 Destruction draws the same line from the other side: its scope note reserves E6 alone for the case where the matter remaining from the destruction is not documented. Here it is documented (the salvaged frame is the point of the record), so E81 is the correct construction.

4. The SIG has discussed the moved-building case twice and read it the same way both times, though neither discussion produced a formal resolution, so treat these as corroboration rather than as rules. In 2015 Martin Doerr argued that 'any "moving" of buildings should be regarded as a "reconstruction"' and that 'we should by rule define such a building as new' regardless of how much old substance it carries (t0821, message 12). In December 2025 he proposed adding to E18's scope note that where moving requires separating at substantially new boundaries, 'a new instance of E18 Physical Object is created that incorporates the previous item', a process to be documented by E81 Transformation (t1874, message 11).

DO NOT MODEL THIS AS E9 MOVE. If the barn is typed correctly the CRM will not let you: P25 moved has range E19 Physical Object, and connect E9 E24 returns no property that could carry a moved barn. For the same reason, avoid P53 has former or current location for the site: the tool reports its full path as running through E19 Physical Object. P25i moved by: E9 Move. P26 moved to: E53 Place, i.e. P53 presupposes exactly the Move that did not happen to this building. Use P156 occupies instead (declared full path: P196 defines: E92 Spacetime Volume. P161 has spatial projection: E53 Place) to attach Hollow Farm to the first barn and Combe Farm to the second.

THE RECORD, CONCRETELY

- Barn A (E24), P156 occupies Hollow Farm. The 1839 tithe survey is an E31 Document that P70 documents Barn A. Everything the survey says stays on Barn A's record.
- The 1938 re-erection, a single event typed (E81, E12) - the dual instantiation the SIG itself uses for the Venetian Loggia, the Hephaisteion and the Dominicanenkerk examples (t1396, t1411). P124 transformed Barn A; P123 resulted in Barn B; P108 has produced Barn B; P4 has time-span 1938; P14 carried out by the estate; P7 took place at both sites. Use P16 used specific object to point at the salvaged fabric. Note that P16 is available only because the event is also an E12 Production: E81 is a subclass of E63/E64 and not of E7 Activity, so P16, P14, P32 and P126 are not on E81 alone. This is a practical reason to assert both classes rather than E81 by itself.
- Barn B (E24), P156 occupies Combe Farm. P128 carries an E34 Inscription whose P190 has symbolic content is 'rebuilt from Hollow Farm barn, 1938'. Modelling the plaque as an inscription on Barn B keeps it where it belongs - as evidence physically present on the later building - instead of silently promoting an estate's wording into an identity assertion.
- The proportion of surviving fabric ('roughly seventy per cent of the original oak frame') belongs in a note (P3 has note) or as an E54 Dimension on Barn B, not in the identity decision. If the survey wants to track the frame itself as a documented thing that persisted through 1938, it can be given its own instance and attached by P46 is composed of to both barns and by P16 used specific object to the 1938 production; but the E81 link already carries the continuity and nothing in the case requires it.

HONEST LIMITS. The CRM supplies the criterion but not the verdict. E12's scope note says in terms that whether an object is regarded as new is context sensitive. Issue 509 (Modifying art objects) was closed in October 2023 without adding any finer classes for the modification/transformation boundary, on the grounds that no supporting datasets had been offered in over three years; and the two mailing-list discussions of moved buildings (t0821, t1874) are both unresolved. So the county survey should write down its own identity rule - e.g. complete dismantling and re-erection on a new site starts a new record, while repair in situ does not - and apply it consistently. What the CRM guarantees is that once you have decided, both records can coexist and the causal and material link between them is expressible without loss.

rejected_alternatives.option: E11 Modification (one continuing building, altered and relocated)
rejected_alternatives.why_not: E11's scope note reserves modification for changes that do not fundamentally change nature or identity, and directs that an event which destroys objects and simultaneously produces others from their parts or material be documented as E81 Transformation, in which case the new items have separate identities. Total dismantling plus a new plinth, new roof and a renewed bay is not an in-situ alteration.

rejected_alternatives.option: E9 Move (the same barn, moved four miles)
rejected_alternatives.why_not: P25 moved has range E19 Physical Object; connect E9 E24 returns no property capable of carrying a moved E24. A timber-framed barn on brick plinths cannot be detached along objective natural boundaries, which is precisely the point Doerr makes in t0821 and t1874. What was moved were the salvaged timbers, not the building.

Its scope note limits E6 alone to the case where the matter remaining from the destruction is not documented. Here seventy per cent of the frame is the documented matter, so the event must also be an E81 Transformation.

rejected_alternatives.option: E79 Part Addition / E80 Part Removal for the new bay, roof and plinth
rejected_alternatives.why_not: E79 and E80 presuppose that the augmented or diminished thing survives the activity as the same identifiable whole (P110 augmented, P112 diminished). Using them would assume the answer to the very question being asked. They are the right classes for later repairs to Barn B in situ, not for the 1938 event.

A genuine option for a fabric-level building survey and a subclass of E24, so it would not change the identity analysis at all; it buys stratigraphic decomposition of the built fabric that this case does not ask for. Adding it here would be padding.

rejected_alternatives.option: E17 Type Assignment / P2 has type change on a single barn record
rejected_alternatives.why_not: E81's scope note explicitly distinguishes transformations from re-classifications documented with E17. Nothing here is a mere reclassification, and the 48th SIG meeting recorded the converse clause - that a change in the use of an object, especially for buildings, does not by itself count as an E81 Transformation.

rejected_alternatives.option: P130 shows features of, to link the two barns
rejected_alternatives.why_not: P130 generalises 'copy of' and 'similar to'. It would record a resemblance between two independent buildings and would lose the causal and material dependence that P123/P124 through a shared event actually assert.

siblings_considered.why_not: E19 Physical Object requires physical boundaries that separate the item completely in an objective way from other objects, and its own scope note says instances can typically be moved. A barn standing on brick plinth walls has no such boundary against its foundations and the ground; typing it E19 would also make P25 moved / E9 Move available and thereby license exactly the 'same building, relocated' reading the case must decide against. The CRM lists comparable structures (the Colosseum, the Palace of Knossos, the Forth Railway Bridge) under E24.

E6 Destruction alone applies when the matter remaining is not documented and the thing simply loses its identity as a subject of documentation. Here the surviving oak frame is documented and re-erected, so the 1938 event must express creation as well as ending - which is what E81, a subclass of both E63 and E64, does and E6, a subclass only of E64, cannot.

E79 Part Addition treats both the augmented thing and the added part as separate identifiable wholes that survive the activity, giving P110 augmented on a persisting building. That presupposes the Hollow Farm barn continued to exist through 1938, which is the disputed point. The 1938 event created a structure, so E12 Production (P108 has produced) is the correct sibling of E11.

E33 Linguistic Object would capture the tithe survey only as an expression in language. What matters here is that the survey makes propositions about the barn, which is E31's defining characteristic and the only route to P70 documents (declared E31 -> E1). E33 offers no equivalent.

E35 Title comprises textual strings identifiable as titles of a thing. 'rebuilt from Hollow Farm barn, 1938' is not the barn's name but a statement affixed to its fabric, which is what E34 Inscription - recognisable texts attachable to instances of E24 - is for.

notes:
The one real friction was verification of quotations. search.py quote accepts thread ids, message ids and document chunk ids, but not concept ids (quote E24 ... and quote E81 ... both return UNKNOWN SOURCE) and not issue ids in any form I tried. The two scope notes that actually decide this case - E24's paragraph on modifying pre-existing things, and E12's remark that newness is context sensitive - are therefore paraphrased rather than quoted, even though both were read verbatim in concept output. I could quote the E81 scope note only because its Issue 404 text was pasted into a mailing-list e-vote (t1396), which is a lucky accident rather than a reliable route. Document chunk ids are only ever exposed indirectly, through the 'search.py quote minutes:...' lines printed by issue <n>; docs output prints section paths but no ids, so there is no general way to quote the specification itself.

Second, the two most on-point mailing-list discussions (t0821 in 2015, t1874 in December 2025) are both unresolved, and t1874's proposed E18 scope-note wording about separating at substantially new boundaries is a proposal, not standard. I have weighted them as corroboration only; the recommendation rests on the current E81, E24, E12, E11 and E6 scope notes and on the closed Issues 386 and 404.

Third, connect printing declared full paths was decisive twice: it exposed that P53 has former or current location is a shortcut running through E9 Move, which is the wrong presupposition for an immobile building, and that P16 reaches the 1938 event only via its E12 aspect, since E81 is not an E7 Activity.
